title: シャボン玉 (Shabon-dama — Soap Bubbles)
description: Soap bubbles fly up to the roof, then shatter and vanish. Born, and immediately broken. The wind: don't blow — let the bubbles fly. A gentle, melancholic song by 野口雨情, believed to be a quiet lament for infant loss. Simple vocabulary, deeply poetic. First published 1922; song arranged 1923. Both creator copyrights (野口雨情 d.1945, 中山晋平 d.1952) expired under Japan's 50-year rule well before the 2018 extension.
